title: Worldwide AI spending forecast, September 2026
observation: Forecast: 2026 total $2,670,460m; infrastructure $1,484,397m; 2027 total $3,637,292m. Search retrieval supplied primary-source text; direct open returned a cache miss. Figures are forecast market context, not BTX-addressable revenues.

title: The cost of compute: a $7 trillion race to scale data centers
observation: $5.2tn AI-related and $1.5tn traditional data-center capital expenditure through 2030 in the central scenario. Cumulative investment, not annual spending; do not add to M01.

title: 2025 AI Index Report
observation: Documents falling costs at fixed capability levels; the report discusses a greater than 280-fold fall in GPT-3.5-level inference cost between November 2022 and October 2024. Historical observation, not a BTX benchmark or 2030 forecast.

title: Instinct MI400 series product specifications
observation: MI455X page lists up to 432 GB HBM4, 23.3 TB/s peak theoretical memory bandwidth and 3.6 TB/s scale-up bandwidth. Vendor specifications; no end-to-end application speedup inferred.

title: Vera Rubin ramps into full production
observation: Vendor announcement reports 10x agent throughput at scale versus its previous platform. Used only as directional evidence of integrated hardware progress.

title: Second-quarter 2026 earnings announcement
observation: Public institutional digital-asset venue analogue. Company report: subscription/services $555m and 48% of net revenue. Case A uses a hypothetical business, not a claim of BTX integration.

title: AI Agent Skills Hub expansion
observation: 13 additional skills spanning trading, payments and institutional functions. Case B borrows the business model of modular agent access, not any proprietary API implementation.

title: Capital Connect institutional programme
observation: Describes institutional investors, professional trading teams and portfolio accounts. No endorsement or available BTX custody is implied.

title: 2025 full-year financial highlights
observation: 2025 company disclosure: $48.2bn assets on platform, 5.7m funded accounts, $2.2bn adjusted revenue; 47% trading and 53% asset-based/other revenue. Shared-infrastructure, custody and wholesale analogue for Case C.

title: Annual Report 2025
observation: Business-account, FX and treasury distribution analogue for Case D. Use business model; hypothetical case numbers are separate.

title: Second-quarter 2026 results
observation: Reports $369bn Total Platform Assets; defines that measure separately from AUC. Describes advisor and agentic-account expansion. Case E is hypothetical.

title: Second-quarter 2026 results
observation: Reports $15.3tn AUM and 13% growth in technology services/subscriptions. AUM belongs to the asset manager; it is not the assets processed by its technology customers.

title: Whole Portfolio product overview
observation: Public/private portfolio views, integrated investment book, exposure, performance and risk. Case F and the institutional guide propose a neutral integration model; there is no proprietary integration or native product-support claim.

title: Studio API solutions
observation: Official overview describes read/write access and operational services including trades, orders and compliance. Detailed customer API contracts are not publicly supplied; this package invents no proprietary endpoint.

title: Studio and data-cloud overview
observation: API-first platform and integration of platform and non-platform data. Supports generic adapter and data-warehouse architectural analysis.

title: x402 introduction
observation: HTTP payment protocol for automated access to APIs/content. Payment rails can pay for more than operating consumption; BTX differentiates the managed object and lifecycle rather than claiming only it can transfer capital.

title: FAPI 2.0 Security Profile
observation: Retain HCP authentication choices and sender constraints. No custom identity stack.

title: OAuth 2.0 security best current practice, RFC 9700
observation: Authorization security baseline for provider-bound tokens.

title: OAuth DPoP, RFC 9449
observation: Sender-binding precedent, not approval of an arbitrary business request body.

title: OAuth Rich Authorization Requests, RFC 9396
observation: Structured authorization; retain exact HCP intent and capital-plan digest checks.

title: FDC3 Context Data 2.2
observation: Desktop context interoperability, private type namespaces and identifier conventions. BTX contexts are custom, not new official FDC3 standard types.

title: FDC3 2.2 standard
observation: Desktop interoperation consists of intents, context, API, directory and agent bridging. Adapters do not gain financial authorization merely by receiving context.

title: Level 2 LEI data: who owns whom
observation: Direct and ultimate accounting-consolidating parents. An LEI relationship is reference data, not authority to debit an entity or proof of every beneficial owner.

title: IAS 38 Intangible Assets overview
observation: Accounting mapping requires actual rights and recognition rules; operational usefulness is not automatic financial NAV.

title: WCAG 2.2
observation: Keyboard, focus, error and accessible-status behavior. Implementation must pass browser accessibility checks.
